zh: 被移动过的数字可以插到任意位置，所以最终答案一定是所有最终数字的升序排列。问题就变成：哪些数字必须被移动（从而加一）。
如果一个数字右边还有比它小的数字，不动它就会挡住那个更小的数字，所以它必须移动一次；移动一次就够了，多移只会让它更大。右边没有更小数字的数字保持原值。
从右往左扫描并维护右侧最小值：当前数字大于这个最小值时，把 min(d+1, 9) 计入计数；否则按原值计数并更新最小值。最后按 0 到 9 的顺序输出各数字的计数，保留前导零。
en: A moved digit can be inserted anywhere, so the final answer is always all final digits in ascending order. The real question is which digits must be moved, and therefore incremented.

If a digit has a smaller digit somewhere to its right, leaving it in place blocks that smaller digit, so it must be moved once; one move is enough, since moving again only makes it larger. Digits with nothing smaller on their right keep their value.

Scan from right to left while keeping the minimum digit seen so far: if the current digit is greater than that minimum, count min(d+1, 9); otherwise count the digit itself and update the minimum. Finally print the counted digits from 0 to 9, keeping leading zeros.

explanationEn:
## Source Mapping

Amazon MERN #5 is labeled in the original as an interleaved algorithm problem and is already included in the main algorithm library. In the fixed snapshot its title is "Optimize Box IDs"; the operation and examples of the Fastprep original are exactly the same as Amazon #34. The link on #5 points to Amazon #13 "Get Total Balanced", which is unrelated to this string problem, so the #5 company number is kept and the verified package of #34 is reused.

## Approach

Scan from right to left while maintaining the minimum digit on the right. If the current digit is greater than that minimum, it must be moved and incremented by 1; otherwise it stays. Finally sort the transformed digits.

## Proof of Correctness

If a digit has a smaller digit after it, not moving it would block the smaller digit from moving forward; an optimal solution can move it and increment it only once, since extra increments are never better. The unmoved digits form a non-decreasing sequence, and moved digits can be inserted at any position, so all digits can be merged in ascending order to obtain the smallest result.

## Complexity

Time O(n+10), space O(n).
